title: The Harbor of Junebug Creek
premise: Jonah Ravensworth is three missed payments from losing his café on the Junebug Creek waterfront when Delia Marsh — the woman who wrote him anonymous letters for a decade from prison — moves into the apartment above his shop after her release. The letters were never love letters; they were confessions about the vineyard empire her family built by framing Jonah's late father for embezzlement, and Delia has spent ten years gathering proof. As their wary friendship deepens into something neither planned, the Marsh family's heir, Cade, returns to town to bury the evidence and buy out the whole harbor block. In the end, Delia and Jonah choose justice outside the courts — exposing the truth at the vineyard's first public harvest festival — and Jonah learns to let someone stay past the last train, keeping both the café and the woman who nearly cost him everything.
about_author: Wendell Quintana spent fifteen years as a line cook in coastal towns before turning to fiction full-time, writing in the off-seasons of shuttered seaside cafés. He lives above a bakery he refuses to name, and claims all his plots arrive by mail.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A bank notice arrives at Ravensworth Café the same morning the health inspector does; Jonah bakes through his panic, feeding regulars who don't know how close he is to losing everything. Emotional beat: quiet desperation masked by routine.

chapters.title: The Woman on the 4:15
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Released after ten years, Delia steps off the train at Junebug Creek with one suitcase and a box of unsent letters, renting the apartment above the café because it was always the plan. Emotional beat: fear braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Letters I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah recognizes his new neighbor as the voice behind a decade of unsigned letters that arrived every birthday — letters he answered but never understood. He confronts her; she gives him nothing but an apology. Emotional beat: disorientation and old grief stirred.

chapters.title: What My Father Built
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia surveys the Marsh vineyard from the ridge road, remembering how her father framed Jonah's father for embezzlement to save the estate. She unpacks her evidence: ledgers, a dead accountant's notes. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Flour and Ashes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A kitchen fire — small, suspicious — forces the café closed for repairs, and Delia shows up with sandbags and steady hands. They work side by side through the night. Emotional beat: first warmth between two guarded people.

chapters.title: The Heir Returns
chapters.summary: Cade Marsh's POV. Cade comes home to manage the harvest and quietly acquire the harbor block, including Jonah's lease. Charming and ruthless, he recognizes Delia at the general store and goes cold. Emotional beat: menace arriving in good tailoring.

chapters.title: Terms of Tenancy
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cade offers Jonah a buyout disguised as rescue; Jonah refuses, not knowing why he trusts the ex-convict next door more than the golden boy. Delia warns him to take the money. Emotional beat: stubborn loyalty against self-interest.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia finally tells Jonah why she wrote: she found the falsified ledgers as a teenager and stayed silent, and the letters were penance. Jonah reads them all in one night. Emotional beat: confession as intimacy.

chapters.title: Harvest Season Opens
chapters.summary: Cade's POV. The vineyard launches its first public harvest festival, a PR campaign to whitewash the Marsh name, and Cade discovers someone has been copying documents from the estate office. Emotional beat: paranoia beneath celebration.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. After a festival gala where Cade publicly humiliates Delia, Jonah asks her to stay — past the last train, past the point of easy retreat. She almost leaves anyway. Emotional beat: the romance crosses its threshold.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia and Jonah reconstruct the fraud together: her father forged Jonah's father's signature weeks before his death. The café becomes a war room of flour dust and photocopies. Emotional beat: partnership solidifying into trust.

chapters.title: A Lawyer Who Owes Me
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They approach a retired county attorney whom Jonah's father once helped, hoping for a legal path. He tells them the statute of limitations has buried the crime — justice must come another way. Emotional beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: Cade's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cade's POV. Cade offers Delia a clean slate and money to disappear, revealing he knows about the copied documents. She refuses; he threatens Jonah's lease and reputation instead. Emotional beat: power corrupting a man who once wanted out.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The café's repaired wiring fails catastrophically before reopening night — insurance voided, savings gone. Jonah suspects Cade but can't prove it. Delia blames herself for bringing the war to his door. Emotional beat: despair and the temptation to quit.

chapters.title: The Accountant's Daughter
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia tracks down the daughter of the dead accountant, who kept her father's hidden originals. The meeting yields the missing page — signed, dated, damning. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into ammunition.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. With the café lost and nothing left to protect, Jonah chooses Delia over safety, telling her they finish this together or not at all. First explicit declaration of love. Emotional beat: devotion without conditions.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Cade's POV. On the eve of the harvest festival, Cade burns the remaining originals in the estate fireplace — unaware Delia already holds copies. His father's portrait watches. Emotional beat: a man becoming what he despises.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Names
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. At the festival's centerpiece ceremony honoring the Marsh legacy, Delia takes the stage uninvited and reads the forged ledger aloud, naming her father and clearing Jonah's father before hundreds of witnesses. Emotional beat: catharsis, public and irreversible.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The town splits; some shun Delia, others bring casseroles and old memories of the wronged Ravensworths. Cade, exposed, signs the harbor block back rather than face a civil suit built on the surviving evidence. Emotional beat: justice landing unevenly but truly.

chapters.title: Reopening
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The community funds the café's true repairs; Delia bakes beside Jonah for the reopening, her first honest work in eleven years. Her father's conviction is formally revisited by a journalist's inquiry. Emotional beat: earned grace.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Cade's POV. Stripped of the estate, Cade works his own small vineyard plot and sends Jonah a letter of his own — an apology, unsigned until now. Emotional beat: the possibility of redemption for the antagonist.

chapters.title: Staying Past the Last Train
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. One year later, on the anniversary of her arrival, Jonah meets the 4:15 train with Delia returning from testifying at the reopened case — and proposes on the platform as the last car pulls away. Emotional beat: second chances, finally well-timed.
